title: Allow Qdrant to run on read-only FS
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

Currently qdrant requires write access to storage directory, even if there are no write operations happening in the system.
It would be interesting in some scenarios to have an ability to run qdrant from read-only FS. For example, from the mounted network FS, so that multiple qdrant instances can serve same data.


**Describe the solution you'd like**

Introduce a new CLI argument `--read-only` which will enable read only mode in qdrant.

For update APIs read-only instance should behave in the same way as for read-only API key - respond with `403 Forbidden` and explanation that the instance is in read-only mode.

Distributed deployment can't be read-only.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Automatic fallback into read-only if the file system doesn't allow writes, but it seems less flexible and error-prone.

**Additional context**

read-only mode assumes skipping WAL reading, so all changes should be applied and flushed to the real storage in advance


---

Note for contributors: Please consider this as tracking issue. If you think that it would be beneficial to split the task into multiple smaller PRs, please you are welcome to do so. Bounty will be rewarded for each PR independently

Just sat down and planned out how this could go, my current plan to start with `src/actix` is to:

- Add the `--read-only` flag, and store its value in the TOC
- Move `is_read_only` and `READ_ONLY_POST_PATTERNS` out of `api_key.rs` to somewhere common in `src/actix`
- Create a new file in `src/actix` with a `ReadOnlyMiddleware` struct with just a boolean member, whose `Service` impl uses a call to `is_read_only` and on failure sends out a HTTP 403 in the same way `api_keys.rs` does

@reporter would this approach be acceptable to you for this PR? I'm hesitant to move something from `api_key.rs` just because the PR for that was so recent, but I figured having the API read only and FS read only mechanisms in the same place and both implemented as Actix middleware made the most sense.

Thanks!

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
I finally articulated out the core issue I was hitting my head against--the way `ApiKey` is written, it expects an `ServiceResponse<EitherBody<_, BoxBody>>` replacing the right variant with the expected HTTP 403 response when an invalid API call is made.

`ApiKey::new()` is wrapped in a `Condition::new()`, which bypasses the wrapped middleware when its predicate is false and puts the result in the right variant. This means the resulting response is of type `ServiceResponse<EitherBody<..., R>>` where `R` is the `Response` type of the middleware wrapped in before `ApiKey`, namely `Compress::default()`.

The reason I can't directly replicate what `ApiKey` does is that because `ApiKey` uses that same type of right variant in the `ServiceResponse<EitherBody>` it receives to stow its HTTP 403 response, it needs the middleware before it to have that right variant be of type `BoxBody`, which doesn't hold true if I add a new middleware below the `.wrap(Condition::new(ApiKey::new(...))`. 

There's a couple paths forward I've found that break symmetry with how `ApiKey` is written but would work. Let me know if you have any preference among these @reporter  and I can go ahead and implement it/look for a better solution: 

1. Skip the use of `Condition::new`, instead just having the new middleware itself check the predicate and skip delivering an error 403 if we're not in read-only mode (simplest)
2. Use an `Either` future or similar, like `CompressMiddleware` [here](https://docs.rs/actix-web/latest/src/actix_web/middleware/compress.rs.html#79-93) and wrap the previous response with it

Thanks so much!
